title: Bringing Multi-Modal Multi-Task Federated Foundation Models to Education Domain: Prospects and Challenges

bias_targets.methodology: The paper does not empirically measure this bias but evaluates it conceptually. It proposes that multi-modal federated foundation models (M3T FedFMs) mitigate the amplification of existing gender biases found in centralized models by enabling distributed, gender-diverse participation in model training.

Evaluated as a theoretical framework; the paper addresses cultural bias by proposing that federated learning allows distributed educational institutions to fine-tune models on culturally specific data, preventing the global model from being skewed toward dominant cultures.

Discussed conceptually; the authors propose mitigating language representation disparities by allowing local institutions to train models using indigenous or low-resource languages, fostering inclusivity compared to centralized models.

Addressed theoretically through the lens of 'Infrastructure/Hardware-Aware Participation.' The paper evaluates how resource and hardware disparities marginalize under-resourced learners, proposing modular federated learning to enable participation from entities with limited computational resources.
